I traced the issue to three files:

- [Container.tsx](/app/packages/components/containers/notifications/Container.tsx:19) renders string `text` as React text, which escapes HTML. String content needs sanitization before HTML rendering, with every link forced to `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. React elements should continue rendering directly.
- [manager.tsx](/app/packages/components/containers/notifications/manager.tsx:63) assigns the ID as the key and deduplicates by string text. It needs to compare a key chosen in this order: explicit key, string text, then ID. Deduplication should apply only to non-success notifications and should not replace an existing success notification.
- [interfaces.ts](/app/packages/components/containers/notifications/interfaces.ts:14) excludes `key` from creation options, so callers cannot provide the explicit key required by the contract.

DOMPurify is already a dependency, and the existing [calendar sanitizer](/app/packages/shared/lib/calendar/sanitize.ts:1) shows an HTML allowlist and link attributes. Its global hook makes direct reuse worth checking. I found no notification-specific tests. I recorded the diagnosis in `.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md`; the assigned fault-localization scope prohibited source and test edits, so the issue remains unresolved in the checked-out code.

Notifications now render string HTML through a restricted sanitizer, and every notification link receives `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. React element content still renders directly. The manager deduplicates non-success notifications by explicit key, then string text, then ID; repeated success notifications remain visible.

Added focused tests. The notification Jest suite, TypeScript check, ESLint, Prettier check, and `git diff --check` all pass.

VERDICT: FIX

- [Container.tsx](/app/packages/components/containers/notifications/Container.tsx:28) can assign the same React key to two visible notifications: a success with ID `1` and an error with text `"1"`. Use distinct rendering keys while retaining the resolved `key` for deduplication.
- [Notification.tsx](/app/packages/components/containers/notifications/Notification.tsx:40) sets link attributes when the parent ref runs. A React child that adds a link later through its own state update can leave that link without `rel` or `target`. Apply the attributes when descendant links are added.

Tests executed: `yarn workspace @proton/components test notifications.test.tsx --coverage=false` passed (2 tests); `yarn workspace @proton/components check-types` passed. **TEST_ENVIRONMENT_PROBLEM:** none. No project code or tests were changed during this review.

Fixed both review findings. Notifications now use their IDs as React rendering keys while keeping the resolved `key` for deduplication. Links added later by React children receive `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and `target="_blank"`.

Added regression tests for both cases. The reviewer’s exact test command passed (4 tests), the component type check passed, and `git diff --check` passed. No remaining failures or test environment problems.
